messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: standar error formula
parts:
Alejandro-

Standard error is a measure of precision for a parameter estimate(estimator)
Standard deviation is a measure of variation of the data around a mean

This can become confusing because texts will use the term standard
deviation of the mean which is really a standard error for the mean. If
s is the standard deviation of the data for n measurements, then the
standard error of the mean is s divided by the square root of n. This
relationship between the standard deviation of the data and the standard
error only holds for an estimated mean. An estimated mean is an estimate
of a parameter (population mean).

The formulas for the standard errors of parameters (square root of the
parameter variance) in distance sampling are given in the Distance
Sampling book. The outputted standard errors do NOT need to be divided
by sqrt(n) if that was the reason for your question.

regards --jeff
